public_discovery_observations.observation: The canonical infotradescout/Selective-Intelligence repository was the first of three repository results.
The canonical repository was absent from the visible exact-name results, and the AI Overview interpreted the phrase as selective attention.

The HTML page, canonical JSON, well-known JSON, llms.txt, robots.txt, and sitemap.xml each returned HTTP 200. Every response was byte-for-byte identical to the corresponding file in main commit 26720ddf9ba849cf8830a9e9ec47952b887874de, and the Pages build record names that exact commit.
The focused exact-name-and-publisher query returned no matching documents immediately after the public bridge was built. Search indexing remains unproven and is monitored rather than claimed.

partial_smoke_observations.loader_observation: After correcting the OpenAI policy products and si-queue-manager frontmatter, the post-fix Codex run emitted no Selective Intelligence metadata or subskill load error.
partial_smoke_observations.limitations: This is a bounded activation smoke matrix, not the complete behavior suite. ChatGPT and Codex are two client surfaces from the same provider and user-level memory remained available. Fresh non-OpenAI evidence now exists, but Gemini and GitHub Copilot failed both cases, including a Copilot Free rerun after the public discovery bridge was live. Claude, Cursor, and Kiro were blocked before a valid seedless run. The evidence therefore disproves current general cross-client and cross-provider equivalence and shows that publication cannot force a general web-chat surface to search or adopt an external skill. One of three Codex discovery finals contained only the exact approval question; its required benefit sentence was visible in the live progress stream before the final message.
